Background.dc.html.title: 10 · Regolith in the background (system, drawn loosely)

t1.text: Upload to a share — try it

play.text:
Press Play, then: Upload (top bar) › Photos & videos › pick a few, including the 612 MB video › Add.

One run rehearses both kinds of trouble. The share drops on the 2nd file and comes back by itself. The video then hits a full share and waits for you: ↻ resumes it from 80%, not from zero.

Tweaks › rehearseFailures off for the clean path.

engine.text: Under it: one queue, one file at a time, rows in the database, so it survives the app closing or the phone rebooting. Bytes go to a .part file on the share, renamed to the real name only when complete, so nobody ever sees half a photo. A retry picks up from the .part's size.

entry.text:
Upload sits in the top bar of any folder on a share, beside rows/tiles. It isn't at the Browse root or in Phone storage: neither is a folder you can upload into.

Picking is the confirm: no review step. You land back in the folder and watch the files arrive where they're going. From any other tab, one line above the pill says how it's going.

photos.text:
DECISION: Browse lists videos only. An uploaded video lands as a normal row. An uploaded photo is on the share but has nowhere to show, so v1 says so under the summary (frame 5).

The alternative is a Photos section in Browse: a new table, thumbnails over SMB, and a viewer.

causes.text:
Two kinds of trouble, handled differently.

The server (share dropped, Wi-Fi gone): the batch waits and resumes by itself from the bytes already sent.

One file (share full, file gone from the phone): that row fails and says why. The rest carry on.

Read-only or a changed password stops the batch and says where to fix it.

Same name, same size: skipped as a copy. Same name, different file: asked once for the whole batch.

location.text: Photo location: Android's photo picker strips GPS from photos, by design. If these uploads are backups, keeping location needs the media-location permission (one more prompt). Worth deciding before the build.
